draft_key_information_units.information: Headline financial performance for 2025 showed revenue declining 7% to €208.3m, gross margin contracting to 6.5% from 7.5%, operating margin falling to 2.7%, net profit shrinking to €2.5m (from €5.2m in 2024), and earnings per share dropping to €0.05 (from €0.12), with profitability impacted by foreign exchange losses.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key figures section; Financial review section; Consolidated statement of comprehensive income

draft_key_information_units.information: Year-on-year segment revenue changes showed the Buildings segment decreasing approximately 10% while the Infrastructure segment increased approximately 10%, resulting in Buildings contributing 81% of total revenue (down from 84%) and Infrastructure 19% (up from 16%).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key figures section; Segment reporting – operating segments (revenue tables)

draft_key_information_units.information: The order book grew by 30% to €273.1m at year-end, driven by a nearly threefold increase in the Infrastructure segment order book; approximately 69% of the backlog relates to work scheduled for 2026, with the remainder spread across 2027-2028.

Cash flows for 2025 included €1.2m net cash from operating activities, €2.8m net cash used in investing activities (including €2.9m placed in long-term deposits), and €1.2m net cash used in financing activities, resulting in a net cash outflow of €2.8m for the year.

Liquidity position at 31 December 2025 was characterized by a current ratio of 0.93 (down from 0.94 in 2024), cash and cash equivalents of €5.3m (down from €8.2m), and short-term borrowings of €12.0m.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Liquidity risk section; Consolidated statement of financial position

draft_key_information_units.information: Net profit was materially affected by a foreign exchange loss of €750k resulting from the Ukrainian hryvnia weakening approximately 12% against the euro during 2025.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial risks section; Note 13 (Finance income and costs)

draft_key_information_units.information: Average employee count remained stable at 431 (274 engineers and technical professionals) in 2025, while staff costs decreased 14% to €21.4m compared to 2024, primarily due to lower performance-based pay.

evaluation.selection_rationale: The draft units focus on material summary-level content directly supporting the evaluation priorities: headline financial performance (D1), major period-over-period changes and performance drivers (D2, D6), key order book developments (D3), liquidity and cash flow dynamics (D4, D5), and operational efficiency (D7). Units exclude routine boilerplate (governance, remuneration, risk lists, accounting policies) and avoid duplication or excessive granularity. Each unit represents an independently omittable theme with explicit source evidence, aligning with the reference summary's emphasis on revenue, profitability, order book trajectory, FX impact, and operational metrics.
